title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol: third — properly a practical decree gifting singular persons grace and glory
pass_a_gloss: Third it is necessary to know that the decree of predestination properly taken denotes, not a universal law showing to all equally by what manner, or by what means, salvation is obtained, or death is incurred: Such as are those, Whoever will have believed, whoever will have persevered in piety, will be saved; and on the contrary, Whoever will not have believed, whoever will not have exercised works of piety, will be damned. But predestination designates a practical decree of God, by which from eternity he established to gift certain singular persons infallibly with singular goods, that is, with efficacious grace and eternal life. So Paul takes predestination in Rom. 8; when he restricts it to certain definite persons, and joins it with glorification by an inseparable bond: so the School of Theologians, which defined it Preparation of grace in the present, and of glory in the future. Those decrees therefore in which it is set forth only generally to what sort of men eternal life will be gifted, to what sort eternal death will be inflicted, while meanwhile nothing is established concerning grace and glory to be given to any singular persons; such decrees, I say, do not express the force and nature of predestination.
pass_b_english: Third: predestination properly taken does not mean a universal law showing all alike how salvation is obtained or death incurred — Whoever believes and perseveres in piety will be saved; whoever does not believe or practice piety will be damned. It designates a practical decree by which from eternity God established to gift certain singular persons infallibly with singular goods: efficacious grace and eternal life. So Paul takes it in Rom. 8, restricting it to definite persons and joining it inseparably with glorification; so the School, which defined it Preparation of grace in the present and of glory in the future. Decrees that only say generally what sort of men get eternal life or death, while settling nothing about grace and glory for any singular persons, do not express predestination's force and nature.
source_text: Tertio cognoscere oportet, praedestinationis decretum proprie sumptum denotare, non legem universalem ostendentem omnibus ex aequo, quo modo, vel quibus mediis, salus obtineatur, aut mors incurratur: Qualia sunt illa, Quisquis crediderit, quisquis in pietate perseveraverit, salvus erit; et contra, Quisquis non crediderit, quisquis opera pietatis non exercuerit, damnabitur. Sed praedestinatio designat practicum Dei decretum, quo ab aeterno statuit singulares quasdam personas singularibus bonis, hoc est, gratia efficaci et vita aeterna, infallibiliter donare. Sic Paulus praedestinationem accipit Rom. viii; quando illam ad quasdam certas personas restringit, et cum glorificatione inseparabili nexu conjungit: sic Schola Theologorum, quae illam definivit Praeparationem gratiae in praesenti, et gloriae in futuro. Decreta ergo illa in quibus exponitur tantum generatim qualibus hominibus vita aeterna donabitur, qualibus mors aeterna infligetur, interim autem nihil statuitur de danda gratia et gloria ullis singularibus personis; talia, inquam, decreta vim naturamque praedestinationis non exprimunt.
